title: Rabbi Avun son of Rabbi Yose
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman records a mention in the edition of the Jerusalem Talmud on Chullin newly printed in his day, at folio 8a. He suggests that the text may instead read “in the name of Rabbi Yose,” or that Avun may have been the son of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun.

notes.text: The supplied title is a Jerusalem Talmud on Chullin, described as newly printed in Hyman’s time, not a new edition being reported today. Its occurrence is unverified here. The compressed בש״ד יוסי is provisionally read בשם ר׳ יוסי, “in the name of Rabbi Yose”; both that reading and Hyman’s alternative filiation remain tentative.

In his 1907 study of Friedländer’s edition, Wilhelm Bacher (Ha-Kedem I.1, p. 25) gives the heading Rabbi Avun son of Rabbi Yose and quotes Chullin 8a, chapter 1, halakhah 4, as “Rabbi Bun son of Rabbi Yose.” He proposes either “Rabbi Avun in the name of Rabbi Yose” or that Rabbi Yose son of Avun had a son named for his grandfather. The National Library of Israel catalogues Friedländer’s edition as a forgery. Bacher’s quotation documents what he read in that edition. The folio itself has not been inspected here. Hyman’s printed abbreviation reads בש״ר, “in the name of Rabbi,” alongside בש״ד in the supplied Hebrew.
